image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) swimming in rippled blue water. The duck is captured from a side-rear angle, showing its iridescent green head, white neck ring, chest/brown breast, and greyish-brown body. The bill is partially visible but mostly obscured by the angle and shadow. The legs and feet are submerged and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is largely occluded by the viewing angle and the duck's posture (head turned away/down). While a hint of yellow/green is visible, the full structure cannot be verified against the 'broad, flat' description.
The eye is visible on the side of the green head and appears dark/black, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a floating duck, appearing streamlined and buoyant. The plumage texture appears dense and waterproof as it sits high on the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the diagnostic mallard drake features: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brownish-grey body plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely submerged beneath the water surface and are not visible.
The folded wing is visible along the side of the body. It appears broad and tapers towards the tail, consistent with the 'pointed' description when folded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear of the duck. While the specific 'curl' of the central feathers is subtle due to the angle and water interaction, the short tail structure is present.
